changes.before: Build a description list with Pickup and Return facts. Return has two descriptions.
changes.after: Connect names with their descriptions in a small list.

before: A description list associates names with descriptions. dl wraps the list, dt supplies a name, and dd supplies its description. Use it for a small glossary or a set of labeled facts, not merely to indent text.

Within the simple pattern here, one dt followed by two dd elements gives two descriptions for that name. A new dt starts the next group. These are not numbered steps; use ol when sequence is the point.

Put this fragment inside body.

```html
<dl><dt>Collection point</dt><dd>East desk</dd><dt>Return time</dt><dd>Before closing</dd></dl>
```

East desk describes Collection point. Before closing describes Return time. The next dt changes which name the following description belongs to.

Give Pickup the description Blue shelf, then give Return both descriptions Friday and Before 4 pm. Keep both return descriptions before any next dt. The checks inspect association through order; they cannot tell whether the real desk accepts returns then.
after:
A description list pairs names with information about them. `dl` holds the list, `dt` gives a name, and `dd` gives a description.

Use it for a glossary or labeled facts, not just to indent text.

In our simple list, a `dt` can have more than one `dd` after it. They all describe that name until the next `dt` begins.

Use an ordered list instead when you mean a sequence of steps.

Put this example inside `body`.
```html
<dl><dt>Collection point</dt><dd>East desk</dd><dt>Return time</dt><dd>Before closing</dd></dl>
```
East desk describes Collection point. Before closing describes Return time. Each `dt` starts a new name group.

Build two groups. Pickup has one description: Blue shelf. Return has two: Friday and Before 4 pm.

Keep the two Return descriptions together after its `dt`.
